transcript:
Doctor: Mr. Whitfield, you mentioned you've been struggling with anxiety. Can you tell me more?
Patient: I've been having panic attacks — my heart races, I feel like I can't breathe, sweating. They come out of nowhere, maybe three or four times a week. I've been avoiding driving on the highway because I had one there.
Doctor: How long has this been going on?
Patient: About four months. It started after I got laid off from my job. I also can't sleep — I lie awake for hours worrying.
Doctor: Any thoughts of harming yourself?
Patient: No, nothing like that. I just feel like things are out of control.
Doctor: Any past history of anxiety or depression? Any medications currently?
Patient: I had some anxiety in college but never treated it. No current medications.
Doctor: I'm going to do a PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Your GAD-7 score is 16 — that's severe anxiety. PHQ-9 is 11 — moderate depression. On exam, you're alert, blood pressure 132 over 84, heart rate 94. Thyroid is non-tender, no goiter. I want to rule out thyroid issues so I'm ordering a TSH.
Patient: Do I need medication?
Doctor: Yes, I think it would help alongside therapy. I'm starting you on sertraline 50mg daily — we'll increase to 100mg after two weeks if tolerated. SSRIs take four to six weeks to show full effect, so don't be discouraged early on. For the panic attacks and sleep, I'm also prescribing a short course of lorazepam 0.5mg as needed, no more than once daily — this is strictly short-term while the sertraline builds up.
Patient: I've heard those can be addictive.
Doctor: You're right to be cautious. We'll use it sparingly and stop it after four weeks maximum. The goal is the sertraline long-term. I also strongly recommend cognitive behavioral therapy for panic disorder — it's as effective as medication. I'll give you a referral.
Patient: Okay. Any lifestyle changes?
Doctor: Limit caffeine, especially after noon. Regular exercise significantly helps anxiety — even a 30-minute walk daily. Avoid alcohol; it worsens anxiety and sleep.
